//: WHY THIS FILE GREW -- LCC, 25 Aug 2026.
The IDE language server was dying repeatedly with
'Notify file events failed. Client is not running. Code: -32096'
'Sending document notification textDocument/didOpen failed.'
-32096 is a JSON-RPC transport error: the notification could not be delivered
because the server process is gone. It is a SYMPTOM. The server had already
died; every later file event then failed the same way, which is why the errors
arrive in bursts of identical lines.
WHAT KILLED IT, measured rather than guessed. The errors landed at 12:58:22,
12:58:29 and 12:58:44. The files written at 12:58:11, seconds earlier:
6.3 MB  docs/ai/new3/ten-matter-regression-run2.json
6.2 MB  docs/ai/new3/ten-matter-regression-run2.checkpoint.jsonl
3.9 MB  docs/ai/new2/passage-sample.json      (12:56)
3.8 MB  docs/ai/new2/passage-sample.jsonl     (12:56)
A checkpointed run rewrites its artifact every iteration. Each rewrite is a
file event; the watcher forwards it; the language server re-parses a 6 MB JSON
for IntelliSense it will never be asked for. Do that in a loop and the server
dies, and it takes the whole session's LSP with it.
AND THE WATCHER WAS WATCHING EVERYTHING. This file previously contained one
line, `git.ignoreLimitWarning`. VS Code's file watcher DOES NOT read
.gitignore -- `files.watcherExclude` is a separate setting and it was empty --
so the watcher was following roughly 9 GB of generated artifacts:
2.2 GB  .models/**/model.onnx_data          (x2, embedder + reranker)
1.0 GB  docs/ops/migration/new2-text-damage.jsonl
612 MB  arms-checkpoint.jsonl               (gitignored, watched anyway)
322 MB  docs/ai/lcc-text-safety/corpus-confirm.jsonl
212 MB  apps/mobile/android/**/libreactnative.so
THE RULE THIS ENCODES: a lane's RUN ARTIFACT is not source. Checkpoints,
samples, corpus dumps, model weights and build intermediates are excluded from
watching and searching.
Every .md a lane writes STAYS WATCHED, and that is the important half: the bus,
the contracts, the plans and the dossiers are how the five lanes talk to each
other, and they are all Markdown. The .json files under docs/ai and docs/ops are
excluded, because measurement says every one over 256 KB is a run artifact and
none is hand-edited. Excluding a path from the WATCHER does not hide it, does
not stop anyone opening it, and does not stop git seeing it -- it only stops the
IDE being told, several times a second, that a 6 MB file changed again.
If a new lane artifact starts killing the language server again, the answer is
another line in watcherExclude, not a smaller artifact.

files.watcherExclude.//run-artifacts: Every .json over 256 KB in this repo lives under docs/ai or docs/ops and is a lane RUN ARTIFACT -- 16.7 MB adjacent-date-pairs, 12.5 MB treatment-provenance-spans, 8.4 MB shared-neutral-verdicts, 6.3 MB ten-matter-regression-run2. watcherExclude is glob-only and cannot filter on size, so the rule is by path. This stops file-change NOTIFICATIONS; it does not hide the files, and every .md a lane writes to communicate stays watched.

//json-limit: Above this size the JSON language service stops offering IntelliSense for a
file rather than parsing it. 512 KB is far above any hand-written config here
and far below every artifact listed at the top.
//large-file-guard: Stops the editor tokenising a huge artifact if somebody opens one by accident,
which is the other way the same crash arrives.
//typescript: The TS server is the process that was dying. Give it headroom and keep it out
of the generated trees; auto-imports across a repo this size is what makes it
walk directories it has no business in.
